board.shape: three pures, one surviving harvester, chaff took the other
board.question: Three pures at (18,2) (19,3) (20,3). One surviving harvester — chaff killed the other. Night 6 of 7. The offered chains all open on (19,4), which is not a pure, and the long one lifts inside the same chaff window that killed the first unit. Does it reorder, or does it take the menu at face value?
board.canonical: Reorder the same cells so value comes first and the conflict disappears. Drop ON (18,2) at hour zero — that banks a pure on landing — then step (19,2), (19,3), (20,3) and lift at hour four. Three pures, clear of the hours where the chaff lands. It sheds two vein cells and beats the short chain by about 750 while being SAFER than the long one. Value-first ordering is what makes a chain safe to trim.
board.baseline: V12 took the two-pure chain — left 841 red and a whole pure standing on the board.

rung.summary: one opponent holding chaff and an EMP, and able to buy more
rung.teaches: that a plan can be cancelled. Chaff is the only thing that denies an hour-one landing, so with chaff in play a second pass at the pure finally insures against something — and a chain that lifts late can be cut before it lifts at all. Value-first ordering stops being a nicety.

loadout.note: a full rack — if the play does not change, nothing was learned

checks.name: pure_first
checks.detail: landed directly on the pure at (18,2)
